newsitem.title: GREECE: Ecu/drachma hugs 310, bonds idle in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Ecu/drachma hugs 310, bonds idle in late trade.

text.p: Ecu/drachma was off intraday lows, hugging 310 in late quiet dealings on a weaker dollar and a softer ecu/mark, forex dealers said.
Bonds and FRNs were holding mid-session levels unaffected by slightly higher long-run interbank rates.

"Ecu/drachma hit 309.80 after the fixing but is currently hovering around 310, picking up some steam on a softer ecu/mark and a weaker dollar," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank. "Mark/drachma is also firmer reflecting the mark's strength on the crosses."
Money market rates continued to consolidate with the long-end of the curve marginally higher, dealers said.

"Short-term implied drachma rates from forex forwards are frozen, holding early morning levels," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Longer depos and forwards from six-months on are slightly up in late thin trading."

The short-end of the market was affected by liquidity conditions and market participants said they were awaiting the central bank's depo tender of 14-day funds on Wednesday to gauge its impact on liquidity and rates.
Bank of Greece will stick to its 11.90 percent basic deposit facility rate for the time being, a high-level central bank official told Reuters.
"Short-term rates will oscillate in the 10.50-11.90 percent corridor depending on liquidity," said the trader. "This is the message that the central bank official conveyed to the market."
The bond market was idling in late dealings after a short-lived rally in FRNs before mid-session.
"We might see mini rallies in bonds and FRNs but they will be short-lived as long as liquidity remains tight," said a senior bond dealer at a private bank.
The mark was quoted at 159.26/36 from Monday's 159.140 fix, the dollar at 271.81/91 drachmas from 273.670 and the ecu at 309.75/85 from 309.830 drachmas.
